rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi links al-Inshiqāq with al-Muṭaffifīn: both warn deniers of recompense and describe two final groups, with right-hand recipients succeeding and left-hand recipients disgraced.
rows.anchor: the rejecters of reward and punishment are warned in the previous sūrah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both sūrahs address affluent people who deny judgment or expect worldly honor in the afterlife; innate awareness of justice and the world's purpose require a final separation, dooming those who ignore it.
rows.anchor: Both sūrahs address the affluent and wealthy sections of the society

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding sūrah reasons from human nature, whereas al-Inshiqāq reasons from signs in the physical world.
rows.anchor: The basis of reasoning in the previous sūrah is human nature

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Judgement the heavens and earth undergo upheaval but obey God without hesitation; obedience is their due because He created them.
rows.anchor: neither the heavens will dare disobey the Almighty nor the earth

words: إِنَّكَ كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَدْحًۭا فَمُلَٰقِيهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man is rebuked for being inexorably drawn toward meeting his Lord and fate; those given their accounts in their right hands will have an easy, happy reckoning.
rows.anchor: Man is rebuked that he is being relentlessly pulled to encounter His Lord

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭāriq is al-Burūj's counterpart: they share a theme, while differing in discourse style and arguments, and their introductions and endings closely resemble each other.
rows.anchor: Both have the same central theme.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Signs in the world, within humans, and in the Creator's attributes establish that Judgement is certain; its delay is respite that removes excuses, and the deniers' end is near.
rows.anchor: should not mislead them to deny it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not hastily seize the arrogant, but when He does, no one can escape His grasp.
rows.anchor: when He does, no one is able to free himself from His clasp.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening oath calls heaven and earth to witness God's all-seeing knowledge; every soul, human and jinn, has a guardian, and none lies beyond God's control or power to seize.
rows.anchor: Heavens and earth are called to witness on the fact that nothing is beyond the eyes of God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human origin is a bodily fluid, not a rare substance beyond God's reach; since He made a living person from it, He can recreate him.
rows.anchor: he is made from a drop of fluid which emanates from his own body.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows deeds, words, heart-secrets, and hidden details; these will be examined on Judgement Day, when no personal support or intercession can help.
rows.anchor: One day, all these secrets shall be examined and assessed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 11–14 invoke a general physical phenomenon to show that the threatened Judgement is certain, not jest, and that people should prepare for it.
rows.anchor: A general physical phenomenon is presented to argue that the Day of Judgement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An earlier argument is said to show that the present order of sūrahs in the muṣḥaf was established in the Prophet's lifetime.
rows.anchor: فهذا يدل على ان ترتيب السور على ما هو عليه في المصحف الآن كان على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some cite letter-count patterns in the Ḥawāmīm and the sūrahs beginning Alif Lām Rā as a divinely grounded reason for sūrah order.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم لترتيب وضع السور في المصحف أسباب تطلع على أنه توقيفي صادر من حكيم الأول يحسب الحروف كما في الحواميم وذوات ﴿ الر ﴾

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some cite the semantic correspondence between a sūrah's ending and the next sūrah's opening, as with al-Fātiḥah's ending and al-Baqarah's beginning.
rows.anchor: الثاني لموافقة آخر السورة لأول ما بعدها كآخر الحمد في المعنى وأول البقرة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some cite verbal rhythm or weight, exemplified by the ending of al-Masad and the opening of al-Ikhlāṣ, as a rationale for the order.
rows.anchor: الثالث الوزن في اللفظة كآخر ﴿ تبت ﴾ وأول الاخلاص

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some cite similarity between a passage in one sūrah and a passage in another, as in al-Ḍuḥā and al-Sharḥ.
rows.anchor: الرابع لمشابهة جملة السورة لجملة الأخرى كالضحى وألم نشرح

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say each sūrah's opening closely suits the previous sūrah's ending, though the relation is sometimes hidden and sometimes clear.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم اذا اعتبرت افتتاح كل سورة وجدته في غاية المناسبة لما ختمت به السورة التي قبلها

rows.speaker: ربيعة
rows.claim: Ibn Abī Shayba reports that Rabiʿa was asked why al-Baqarah and Āl ʿImrān, both Medinan, preceded more than eighty earlier-revealed Meccan sūrahs; he answered that they were placed first through the compiler's knowledge, which the community shared, and this was not to be questioned.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن ربيعة أنه سئل لم قدمت البقرة وآل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suyūṭī limits the dispute to order within four sūrah categories; the categories' order—long sūrahs, miʾūn, mathānī, then mufassal—is certainly divinely fixed and should be held by consensus.
rows.anchor: وأما نفس الأقسام الأربعة من تقديم الطوال ثم المئين ثم المثاني ثم المفصل فهذا ينبغي أن يقطع بأنه توقيفي وأن يدعى فيه الإجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As evidence for that category order, Suyūṭī notes that the muṣḥafs of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and Ibn Masʿūd, despite other ordering differences, also place the long sūrahs, mathānī, and mufassal as in ʿUthmān's muṣḥaf.
rows.anchor: فإن مصحف أبي بن كعب وابن مسعود كلاهما قدم فيه الطوال ثم المثاني ثم المفصل كمصحف عثمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suyūṭī prefers al-Bayhaqī's view that the order of every sūrah is divinely fixed except al-Anfāl and Barāʾah.
rows.anchor: فالمختار عندي في ذلك ما قاله البيهقي وهو أن ترتيب كل السور توقيفي سوى الأنفال وبراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites the consecutive Ḥawāmīm and Alif Lām Rā groups, and the separation among the Musabbiḥāt, as signs of purposeful, divinely fixed sūrah order.
rows.anchor: ومما يدل على ذلك ويؤيده توالي الحواميم وذوات الر والفصل بين المسبحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing Ṭā Sīn before al-Qaṣaṣ and separating it from the paired Ṭā Sīn Mīm sūrahs reflects their shared opening and relative length.
rows.anchor: وتقديم طس على القصص مفصولا بها بين النظيرتين [ طسم الشعراء وطسم القصص ] في المطلع والطول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Muṭaffifīn separates al-Infiṭār and al-Inshiqāq, although the latter two resemble each other in opening and subject and are longer than al-Muṭaffifīn.
rows.anchor: وكذا الفصل بين الانفطار والانشقاق بالمطففين وهما نظيرتان في المطلع والمقصد وهما أطول منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that without a divinely fixed order for wisdom, the Musabbiḥāt would be consecutive, Ṭā Sīn would follow al-Qaṣaṣ, and al-Muṭaffifīn would not separate the similar alif-lām-rā sūrahs.
rows.anchor: فلولا أنه توقيفي لحكمة لتوالت المسبحات وأخرت طس عن القصص وأخرت المطففين أو قدمت ولم يفصل بين الر و الر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suyūṭī praises the Qur'an as divinely arranged with profound wisdom, a superb system, eloquent wording, and forceful composition.
rows.anchor: ورتبه بحكمته البالغة أحسن ترتيب ونظمه أعظم نظام بأفصح لفظ وأبلغ تركيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He describes sustained exploration of the Qur'an's fields and extraction of its sciences, which he collected in works of varied scope.
rows.anchor: فلا أزال أسرح النظر في بساتينه من نوع إلى نوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asrār al-Tanzīl investigates Qur'anic styles and wonders, eloquence, figurative expression, and the exposition of its arguments and proofs.
rows.anchor: كتاب أسرار التنزيل الباحث عن أساليبه المبرز أعاجيبه المبين لفصاحة ألفاظه وبلاغة تراكيبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book examines relationships among sūrahs and the wisdom behind placing each one where it is.
rows.anchor: الأول بيان مناسبات ترتيب سوره وحكمة وضع كل سورة منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It argues that each sūrah explains what the preceding sūrah stated concisely.
rows.anchor: الثاني بيان أن كل سورة شارحة لما أجمل في السورة التي قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It studies how al-Fātiḥah's opening relates to the ending of the preceding sūrah.
rows.anchor: الثالث وجه اعتلاق فاتحة الكتاب بخاتمة التي قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It studies the suitability of each sūrah's opening to its purpose, the rhetorical art of a fitting introduction.
rows.anchor: الرابع مناسبة مطلع السورة للمقصد الذي سيقت له وذلك براعة الإستهلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It studies the relationship between the beginnings and endings of sūrahs.
rows.anchor: الخامس مناسبة أوائل السور لأواخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It examines verse order and the connections, interrelation, cohesion, and harmony among verses.
rows.anchor: السادس مناسبات ترتيب آياته واعتلاق بعضها ببعض وارتباطها وتلاحمها وتناسقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It describes Qur'anic rhetorical styles and variations in address and discourse.
rows.anchor: السابع بيان أساليبه في البلاغة وتنويع خطاباته وسياقاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It catalogs rhetorical embellishments and figurative devices, including metaphor, metonymy, insinuation, shifts, double entendre, wordplay, antithesis, comparison, majāz, concision, and expansion.
rows.anchor: الثامن بيان ما اشتمل عليه من المحسنات البديعية على كثرتها كالإستعارة والكناية والتعريض والإلتفات والتورية والاستخدام واللف والنشر والطباق
